text:
simon: quick brain-dump: proposal for a per-tenant regional edge gateway that enforces residency but can optionally accept 'escrowed' writes during partitions. want fast feedback on safety and ops tradeoffs.

maria: can you outline how this differs from the existing residency proxy? :thinking:

simon: differences: 1) gateway is the tenant's regional ingress and owns local decisions. 2) when the global write lease is unreachable, it can either reject or accept escrowed writes depending on tenant policy. 3) escrow stores encrypted signed intents (small op logs) not full DB snapshots. aim is to keep cross-region IO low for inference-heavy workloads.

nisha: who reconciles and how do we avoid split-brain? letting both regions accept writes seems dangerous.

alex: safety model is lease-first. normal flow: local gateway forwards to lease-holder region. fallback: if lease check times out (configurable window), and tenant policy allows, gateway accepts escrowed writes with monotonic seq numbers + signed intent envelope. on recovery, reconciliation replays intents in seq order, using deterministic merge rules. non-idempotent conflicts escalate to a human review path.

patrick: keep escrow payloads tiny: intent metadata + op-type + tombstone marker for deletes. no full table shipping. use per-tenant LSN to order.

simon: rough config (pseudo):
```
routing_policy:
  residency: required # required | preferred | none
  failover_behavior:
    allow_degraded_writes: false
    escrow_backend: regional-kv
    escrow_retention: 72h
    reconcile_strategy: monotonic-lsn
    max_escrow_size: 50MB
```

maria: e2e tests? need long partition sim, model rollout during partition, and reconciliation correctness tests. also measure read latency during degraded mode.

devops-bot: preview deployment for "edge-gateway/escrow" created  https://deploys.internal/edge-gateway/escrow-rc4 :rocket:

nisha: security concerns: escrow encryption, KMS policies, and auditability.

simon: escrow payloads envelope-encrypted with tenant KMS keys (HSM recommended). central audit receives only metadata/events; payload stays regional until reconciliation. intents are signed so we can prove provenance.

alex: propose SLOs: local reads <= 50ms P95, remote fallback reads <= 200ms P95, normal writes <= 100ms, degraded-write accept <= 150ms (client-visible); reconciliation target: 24h typical, 72h worst-case for heavy partitions.

patrick: SDK surface: explicit opt-in flag `allow_degraded=true`. server should return header `X-Redwood-Write-Mode: degraded|forwarded|rejected`. default behavior: fail if residency policy forbids degraded writes.

maria: add metrics: `escrow.ops`, `escrow.size_bytes`, `reconcile.attempts`, `reconcile.conflicts`. daily tenant report for degraded writes.

simon: ops note: reconciliation pipeline first runs a lightweight conflict detector (LSN gaps, op counts) and only triggers manual review for non-idempotent conflicts. inference workloads mostly append-only so conflicts rare.

nisha: legal tenants must be able to opt out (disallow degraded writes entirely).

simon: agreed. `residency: required` + `allow_degraded_writes=false` -> write attempts return 409 with human-readable error.

maria: next step: convert to RFC with dataflow diagrams, reconciliation pseudocode, security checklist, and test matrix. I'll co-author. :thumbsup:

simon: will draft RFC today and tag reviewers. thanks all.
